terra.problem: Calling Korah the one behind it all assigns him a role the passage does not specify. It says he conducted the rebellion along with others.
The text does not say Moses gets back up before speaking to Korah.
Saying Moses does not need new words is inaccurate. His response adds words identifying the sons of Levi.
Calling it the same line overlooks the words Moses adds. The two statements are not an exact match.
Moses says they have conspired against the LORD and grumbled against Aaron. Saying the target is the LORD, not Aaron, obscures that distinction.
Calling Aaron an afterthought adds an impression about Moses' treatment of him that the text does not give.
The claim that someone's memory has been edited assigns a reason for their description that the text does not give.
The claim that one would expect them to remember the wilderness for famine is unsupported by the passage.
The last two sentences repeat the accusation without adding an explanation or much of Papa Dorin's voice.
Moses says he has not taken one donkey or mistreated them. Saying he has done nothing to them goes beyond his words.
Moses says he has not taken one donkey, not that he took none of their animals.
Moses presents the unprecedented event conditionally. The explanation turns it into an unconditional prediction.
Moses presents the unprecedented event conditionally. The explanation turns it into an unconditional prediction.
The text does not describe a silence after Moses speaks. Marking it as a guess does not establish that scene detail.
The explanation links the people's flight at the cries to Moses' earlier instruction to move away. The passage describes them moving away before the ground opens.
The joke about their feet makes light of people fleeing at the cries of those being swallowed by the earth.
The broader claim that the priesthood belongs to Aaron's line needs a reference. This passage states the restriction on approaching to offer incense.
Eleazar had the censers hammered out. The text does not say he personally hammered them.
